summary: Set 109 Session 3 of 4, "A pricing schema that can be true, and scrape-to-propose". SHIPPED: `ai_router/pricing.py` -- a model entry declares rates EITHER as the two flat scalars (unchanged, still right for the single-rate majority) OR as a `pricing:` list of rows carrying an optional inclusive `max_input_tokens` and an optional `effective_from`, never both on one entry. Rows sharing a date form a period, so tiers and dates compose with NO nesting -- departing from both routed designs, one of which proposed periods-containing-tiers and the other a min/max token pair whose off-by-one boundary is a bug waiting to be written. Validation runs at CONFIG LOAD and fails closed; notably a period with no unbounded row is REJECTED, because without one a prompt larger than the largest bound would have no rate at all and cost nothing -- the exact class of silent under-reporting this set exists to end. `true` is rejected as a rate, unknown row keys are rejected rather than ignored (a typo'd `max_input_token` would silently widen a tier), and each period is checked independently. ALL SIX CONSUMERS WIRED: `_calculate_cost` resolves the row from the call's own input_tokens and today's date with NO signature change at any of its five call sites (each already passed input_tokens, which is exactly what selects the tier); the three SELECTION paths (verifier tiebreak, escalation fallback x2) rank by `worst_case_output_cost_per_1m`, because they choose before output length or a future billing date is known -- "cheapest available" would make a tiered model look cheaper than it can bill and "the rate in force today" would silently reorder the candidate list on a calendar boundary with no code change; `pull_verifier._pricing_for` and `report._opus_pricing` take the worst case for the same reason, both resolving one rate pair before any token count exists, where a cost CAP that reads low is the one direction that must not happen. ALSO SHIPPED: `ai_router/pricing_proposal.py` -- `--fetch` parses the three published pages and writes a proposal with every change marked "pending"; `--apply` REFUSES while any change is pending and writes only what a human marked "accept", stamping `confirmed_on` on exactly those entries. The acceptance mechanism (edit a decision in a file) departs from BOTH routed designs: print-only cannot satisfy the spec's "only acceptance writes the value and stamps confirmed_on" because there is no acceptance step to hang the stamp on, and an interactive [y/N] CLI needs a TTY so it could only ever be exercised by the operator walking it -- the one place this set cannot afford an unexercised path. Parsing is stdlib html.parser, adding no dependency, and not by preference: the Google page emits UNESCAPED `<= 200k tokens` inside cells and the obvious `<[^>]+>` strip swallows the tier boundary, leaving a plausible single price. ruamel.yaml is lazily required at --apply only, mirroring migrate_router_config, so the comment-preserving dep stays in the optional extra it already lives in. THE LIVE RUN FOUND A DEFECT THE SPEC NEVER NAMED: `gpt-5-5` records $2.50/$15.00 and OpenAI publishes $5.00/$30.00 -- a SECOND 2x understatement with a DIFFERENT cause from gpt-5-6's, since gpt-5.5 is a real id S1's drift gate passes; its rates were copied from gpt-5.4 at authoring time and its own note says PLACEHOLDER in as many words. I COUNTED THE LEDGER BEFORE PUBLISHING THE CLAIM and corrected my own first draft: exactly ONE gpt-5-5 row at $0.0003, so the spend impact is negligible and that is luck, not design -- it was briefly the pinned verifier and the pin moved before it saw use. While counting, found the spec's reconciliation figure is an order of magnitude too small: it cites Set 108 S4's slice ($0.5916 -> $1.18), but the whole ledger holds 245 gpt-5-6 rows totalling $48.95 reported, so the true figure is ~$97.90 and lifetime routed spend is understated by ~$49. gpt-5-4's $2.50/$15.00 was CONFIRMED CORRECT against the page, so its 466 rows need no correction. NO RATE IN router-config.yaml WAS EDITED, deliberately: this set's rule is that a human confirms every rate change, and the flow that makes that possible only exists as of this session, so hand-editing five rates here would have meant breaking the rule in the act of implementing it. S4 walks it. DEPARTURE FROM THE SPEC, DECLARED: `metadata.pricing_reviewed` was KEPT rather than replaced. Grepping before deleting found the VS Code Cost Dashboard renders its staleness banner from that exact field, and "no Explorer or extension work" is an explicit NON-GOAL of this set -- removing it would have broken a shipped surface this session may not touch. It survives as a rollup maintained by --apply. Surfaced for Step 9. AN INFRASTRUCTURE FIX THE SESSION HAD TO MAKE TO FINISH: google and openai carried `timeout_seconds: 300` while anthropic has always had 600. A tier-3 model reasoning at high effort over a large bundle exceeds 300s routinely -- it cost this session two routed architecture calls AND TWO WHOLE VERIFICATION ROUNDS (3 attempts x 300s each, paid for, returning nothing but "The read operation timed out"). Verification is mandatory on every Full-tier session, so a transport ceiling that cannot complete it on a substantial diff is a correctness problem, not a comfort setting. Raised to 900s. VERIFICATION -- SIX ROUNDS, AND THE HONEST SHAPE OF THEM: round 1 discovery (2-way fan-out, gpt-5-6, anthropic excluded) returned 7 blocking; round 2 supplementary returned VERIFIED with NOTHING NEW, so 7 was the complete set. The 7 were 5 distinct defects (1==4, 3==7), ALL ACCEPTED, NONE DISPUTED -- and three of them were fail-open paths that manufacture a plausible-looking number, i.e. precisely what the module docstring promises never to do. Rounds 3, 4 and 5 each returned exactly 1 blocking finding, every one on the SAME SEAM (how a Google parse failure is classified) and every one accepted. Rounds 4 and 5 were taken under the operator's explicit pre-authorisation past the 2-cycle bound. Round 6 was the constitution's THIRD-PROVIDER opinion (google/gemini-3-1-pro, both other providers excluded) and produced the best structural finding of the set: rounds 3-5 all guarded the shape that SURVIVED parsing, while a parse failure most often manifests as a DICTIONARY MISS, which took the deliberately non-fatal "absent from the page" branch. Both remaining parsers (OpenAI, Anthropic) `continue`d past a row they could not read -- the identical fail-open, in the two parsers three rounds of findings had never examined. Fixed at both sites in one pass (L-069-1). Round 6 also judged round 5 an OVER-CORRECTION and was right: requiring every non-blank line in a price cell to parse means an ordinary footnote aborts the run, so the rule is now "a line containing $ that cannot be read is fatal; a line with no $ is prose". TWO OF ROUND 6'S FINDINGS WERE REJECTED WITH REASONS: "make absent fatal" would abort every run on gpt-5.6, which OpenAI genuinely does not list -- a REGISTRY defect S1 built a gate for and S4 fixes, not a parser failure; and its Critical on Anthropic versioned ids is vacuous against this registry (all four ids derive correctly, asserted by test) and the outcome is VISIBLE (reported NOT CHECKED), so it is a documented residual, not a Critical. EVERY finding across all six rounds was in ONE module and, bar the effective-date ordering, on ONE question. Nothing in six rounds touched pricing.py, the six wired consumers, the cost calculation, the schema validation, or any rate in router-config.yaml. SUITE: 3398 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected, 0 failed (21m19s); delta from S2's 3257 baseline is +141, exactly the new tests, with no existing test changed, removed or newly skipped. Two FALSIFIER checks performed and restored: reverting `_calculate_cost` fails the wiring test, and flipping the sort scalar to cheapest-available fails two more. Gates: drift_guard OK, tutorial_gate OK, guidance_report OK (10,895/12,000), model_inventory --check still exits 1 on the gpt-5.6 and gemini-3-pro specimens by design. Router-side only, [Unreleased] in the changelog -- no version bump, no publish, no extension work. VERDICT TOKEN: WAIVED, on an OPERATOR-DIRECTED close attested in s3-close-attestation.md (the operator directed closure three times in writing and pre-authorised the exact round budget, which was spent in full: rounds 4-5 on gpt-5-6, round 6 on a third engine google/gemini-3-1-pro, then three further close-backstop rounds of which 7 and 8 were FIXED rather than waived). What is waived is ONE Major from the final backstop round: once a human hand-encodes OpenAI long-context tiers, a later --fetch would propose replacing that schedule with the flat short-context rate -- a direct consequence of the deliberate round-1 decision never to invent the boundary OpenAI does not publish, and not reachable until someone encodes such a tier, which no entry has today. Owed to S4 with the other residuals. Every finding across all six rounds was either FIXED in-session (16 of 18) or REJECTED WITH WRITTEN REASONS in s3-remediation-round-1.md (2, both from round 6). No finding was left unresolved and unaddressed. What this token does NOT claim is a final clean re-verify: the operator pre-authorised closing after the round budget was spent (2 extra rounds on the current engine, 1 on a third engine), and all three were used, so the round-6 fixes ship reviewed by tests and a live run but not by a further verifier round. That is the honest residual and it is the operator-authorised close, not a self-authorised one.

reason.specifics: Recorded as the ROUTED analyst's recommendation, per the repo rule never to self-opine on model choice -- BUT THE ANALYST RETURNED A MODEL ID THAT DOES NOT EXIST: "Claude 3 Opus" / claude-3-opus-20240229, which is in neither this registry nor at the provider. It is read as claude-opus-5 / high, which is also the right call on the merits: S4 walks a HUMAN confirmation flow (the set's UAT), adjudicates model pins, authors the UAT checklist, and runs the set-terminal Step 9 and path-aware critique -- judgement-heavy work under a hard human-in-the-loop rule. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE SESSION in which the step-3.5 analyst has emitted a non-existent model id, so the routed recommendation this repo relies on in order not to self-opine is itself unvalidated. A route()-side fix -- validate a recommended model id against the registry before returning it -- is owed, and is now CHEAP, because ai_router/model_inventory.py already knows every id each provider offers. Two further facts for S4: (1) gpt-5-4 and gpt-5-6 are what this set's Anthropic-excluded verification rounds fall through to, so orchestrating S4 from either would collapse the cross-provider independence its verdicts rest on -- the same ground on which S2's routed recommendation of gpt-5-4 was not adopted for S3; (2) the Copilot seat budget is very limited, so any engine switch draws on the DABBLER_* keys, not the seat.
